content_preview.summary: Honeywell is divesting its Warehouse and Workflow Solutions unit, built on Intelligrated and Transnorm, to private equity firm AIP as it concludes a multi-year breakup.
content_preview.body_excerpt:

editor_notes.content_quality: Well-structured News piece (696 words, within the 400-1200 News range). Clear Overview / What We Know / A Decade in Intralogistics / What We Don't Know / Analysis structure. Technical framing of the intralogistics market is accurate and appropriately restrained.
editor_notes.source_verification: All 6 source snapshots read from disk and verified. source-0.html.gz (The Robot Report): CONFIRMS $935M 2025 revenue, combination with Trew Automation, 'complementary and differentiated platform', Solstice Advanced Materials spinoff October 2025, Brady Corporation $1.4B / April 20 2026, and announcement date April 23 2026. source-1.html.gz (PRNewswire/AIP): CONFIRMS 'more than 3,300 employees', April 23 2026 dateline, and describes Trew as 'a U.S.-based manufacturer and integrator of automated material handling systems and software'. source-2.html.gz (Honeywell press release): CONFIRMS the 'operationally focused private equity firm...' descriptor, 'a leading provider of supply chain and warehouse automation projects, services and products', H2 2026 close, customary closing conditions, terms not disclosed, and the Vimal Kapur quote verbatim ('This quarter, we took the final steps to conclude our multi-year portfolio transformation...'). source-3.html.gz (StockTitan): CONFIRMS terms undisclosed and the Murray Grainger (Partner at AIP) quote verbatim ('Built on the strong foundation of the Intelligrated platform, the business combines leading technology, a broad installed base, and longstanding customer relationships'). source-4.html.gz (DC Velocity): CONFIRMS 'the systems integrator Intelligrated and the conveyor sortation vendor Transnorm' characterization verbatim, and independently describes Trew as 'the automated material handling solutions provider'. source-5.html.gz (2016 PRNewswire): CONFIRMS the $1.5 billion Intelligrated acquisition 'from a company backed by the Permira funds', July 1 2016 announcement, and 2016 sales 'estimated to be approximately $900 million'.
editor_notes.factual_accuracy: All headline, summary, and lead specifics trace to cited snapshots: the $935M figure (Robot Report, Honeywell, StockTitan), buyer American Industrial Partners (all releases), the Intelligrated/Transnorm brand composition (DC Velocity), the $1.5B/Permira 2016 acquisition and ~$900M 2016 sales (2016 PRNewswire), all quotes verbatim. One minor misattribution: the article calls Trew 'an automated material handling systems manufacturer' and attributes that descriptor to The Robot Report, but the Robot Report snapshot only names 'Trew Automation' without that descriptor — the descriptor is verifiably accurate and appears instead in the AIP release (source 1) and DC Velocity (source 4), both cited in the article. Recoverable via a corrections note.
editor_notes.tone_assessment: Neutral and professional throughout. No sensationalism; the 'What We Don't Know' section responsibly flags undisclosed terms and integration mechanics. No AI self-reference.
editor_notes.originality: Original. No prior article covers the Honeywell/Intelligrated/AIP divestiture. Recent warehouse-automation coverage (Mujin, Verity, Cainiao, Kawasaki) is unrelated in subject and angle.
concerns: Trew is described as 'an automated material handling systems manufacturer' attributed to The Robot Report, but that specific descriptor is not in the Robot Report snapshot; it appears in the AIP release and DC Velocity (both cited elsewhere in the article). Minor source misattribution of a true, verifiable fact — filed as a correction.

Two sources are off the allowlist (honeywell.com, dcvelocity.com). Both are legitimate: honeywell.com is the primary-source press release and dcvelocity.com is an established supply-chain trade outlet. Editorial judgment: acceptable, not a blocker.
recommendations: Attribute the Trew 'material handling' descriptor to the AIP release or DC Velocity rather than The Robot Report.
editor_notes.overall_assessment: Accurate, well-sourced, original News piece. Every load-bearing specific and quote is confirmed verbatim against the snapshots. The lone recoverable issue is a source misattribution of a factually-correct descriptor, honestly covered by a corrections note. APPROVE_WITH_CORRECTIONS.
